module_title: Language Translators - Assembly, Compilers, and Interpreters
introduction: This intermediate tier focuses on one of the most highly tested topics in SSC and Banking exams: Language Translators. We will differentiate between Assembly language mechanics and the critical execution differences between Compilers and Interpreters.

core_concepts.title: Assembly Language (2nd Generation)
core_concepts.description: A step slightly above pure Machine Language. Instead of writing endless 0s and 1s, programmers use short English abbreviations called 'Mnemonics' (e.g., ADD for addition, SUB for subtraction). It is a Low-Level language and is highly hardware-dependent.

core_concepts.title: Assembler
core_concepts.description: A specific software translator whose ONLY job is to convert 'Assembly Language' (Mnemonics) into 'Machine Language' (Binary).

core_concepts.title: Compiler
core_concepts.description:
A translator that reads the ENTIRE High-Level Language program at once. It translates the whole source code into machine code in a single batch. It is very fast in execution but displays all errors at the very end. 
Examples of compiled languages: C, C++.

core_concepts.title: Interpreter
core_concepts.description:
A translator that reads and executes High-Level Language code strictly 'Line-by-Line'. If it finds an error on line 5, it completely stops and forces the programmer to fix it before moving to line 6. It is easier for debugging but slower in overall execution. 
Examples of interpreted languages: Python, Ruby.

important_entities.name: Object Code
important_entities.significance: Once a Compiler successfully translates the human-written Source Code, the resulting machine-readable binary file is called Object Code (or Machine Code).

important_entities.name: Syntax Error
important_entities.significance: Just like English has grammar rules, programming languages have 'Syntax'. If you forget a semicolon or misspell a command, the Compiler will throw a Syntax Error and refuse to translate.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: If a statement-based question asks, 'Does an Assembler translate C++ into machine code?', the answer is strictly NO. Assemblers ONLY translate Assembly Language. C++ requires a Compiler.

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Use 'C' for Compiler and Complete (translates the complete page at once). Use 'In' for Interpreter and In-Line (translates line-by-line).

exam_strategy_tips: The most repeated question in SSC IT sections is: 'Which translator converts code line-by-line?' Without hesitation, mark 'Interpreter'.
